sites.name: Sydney Opera House
sites.fact: Designed by Jørn Utzon and opened in 1973, ten years later than planned. Its shells are covered in more than a million tiles.
sites.hint: The white sails on the point east of the Harbour Bridge.

sites.name: Sydney Harbour Bridge
sites.fact: Opened in 1932. Locals call the steel arch the Coathanger; its top is 134 metres above the water.
sites.hint: The steel arch across the harbour, beside the Opera House.

sites.name: Bondi Beach
sites.fact: About a kilometre of sand on the Pacific. Its surf lifesaving club, founded in 1907, is among the oldest in the world.
sites.hint: The crescent beach on the ocean, east of the city.

sites.name: Sydney Tower
sites.fact: At 309 metres, the tallest structure in Sydney. It opened to the public in 1981.
sites.hint: The golden turret on a thin shaft in the middle of the city.

sites.name: Darling Harbour
sites.fact: Once a busy cargo port, rebuilt as a waterfront of museums, parks and promenades for Australia's bicentenary in 1988.
sites.hint: The narrow inlet on the western side of the city centre.

sites.name: Taronga Zoo
sites.fact: Opened in 1916 on the north shore of the harbour. Many visitors arrive by ferry.
sites.hint: On the wooded north shore, across the water from the Opera House.

sites.name: Manly
sites.fact: A beach suburb on a neck of land between the harbour and the ocean, half an hour by ferry from the city.
sites.hint: Near North Head, at the northern side of the harbour entrance.

sites.name: Royal Botanic Garden
sites.fact: Established in 1816, which makes it the oldest scientific institution in Australia.
sites.hint: The gardens around the bay just east of the Opera House.

sites.name: Sydney Cricket Ground
sites.fact: Cricket has been played on this ground since the middle of the 1800s.
sites.hint: The stadiums in Moore Park, south-east of the centre.

sites.name: Sydney Airport
sites.fact: In use since 1920, one of the oldest continuously operating commercial airports in the world. Two of its runways reach out into Botany Bay.
sites.hint: On the north shore of Botany Bay, south of the city.

sites.name: South Head
sites.fact: The southern headland of the harbour entrance. The red and white Hornby Lighthouse has guided ships in since 1858.
sites.hint: The tip of the peninsula past Watsons Bay, facing North Head.

sites.name: Sydney Olympic Park
sites.fact: Built for the 2000 Olympic Games on former industrial land beside the Parramatta River.
sites.hint: Far up the Parramatta River, west of the city.
